elements.evidence: The added language expressly permits Customer to terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience.

elements.element: Customer may exercise the convenience-termination right on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires 30 days' prior notice.

elements.element: Customer's convenience-termination notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The notice is expressly required to be written.

elements.element: Vendor must refund prepaid fees following Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Vendor is expressly required to provide a refund of prepaid Fees.

elements.element: The refund must be pro-rated for the period after the effective date of termination.
elements.evidence: The clause requires a pro-rata refund for the period after termination becomes effective.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that Vendor may not terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term.
The added language expressly grants Customer a convenience-termination right.

elements.element: Customer must provide at least 60 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The clause requires only 30 days' notice, which is below the fallback minimum of 60 days.

elements.element: Customer's required notice period may not exceed 90 days.
elements.evidence: The stated 30-day notice period does not exceed 90 days.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee may not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no early-termination fee, so no fee exceeds the cap.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination for convenience may take effect only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Vendor is expressly barred from terminating for convenience during a committed term, thereby limiting any permissible exercise to the term boundary.

elements.element: Vendor must provide 90 days' notice of any termination for convenience.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no 90-day notice requirement for Vendor and does not categorically eliminate every possible term-end convenience-termination right.

result.reason: The redline cleanly implements every preferred requirement without altering the existing cause-based termination rights or adding unrelated obligations. It does not independently satisfy the fallback because Customer's notice period is only 30 days and no 90-day Vendor notice requirement is included. The added paragraph is substantively clear, though numbering it as Section 9.4 would improve integration.
